Best Overall Nutrition Ap. I started using My Net Diary over 2 years ago when the app I had been using stopped working, then went behind a paywall. Having suddenly lost access to my account history on that app and several years of records, and having grown frustrated with the cumbersome process of entering the foods I ate, I decided to explore some different apps if I had to start over. 

I saw good reviews for MyNetDiary and started using it. I was using it more for its nutritional tracking capabilities than for weight loss, due to a medical issue with my heart. Having the ability to track protein, fat, cholesterol, and other nutrients was vital to my situation. After using the free version for a several months, I upgraded to the paid version because it allowed me to track salt intake along with the other nutrients I was tracking. I’m not sure why tracking salt was excluded from the free version, but it was. 

I love how easy MyNetDiary is to use, especially the ability to scan the bar code on foods and easily capture and track calories and nutrition information. I found more and more convenient features the longer I used the app. 

I have even documented some foods that were not in the food database, and the people who administer the app added them within just a few days after I reported them. That level of response and support is really rare, and I really appreciate it. 

I have also entered in many recipes for meals I cook and can easily track my meals any time I prepare those same meals. 

I also use the GPS exercise feature that tracks my time and mileage when I go cycling, and lets me import the calorie burn into the app. 

There are lots of other features I have not even used yet, and I will probably explore some of them in the future. 

I just had my 2nd annual renewal after the initial upgrade to the paid version, so I am now starting my 3rd year as a paid subscriber. 

The only thing I wish this app would do is better integrate with off-brand sports watches. It does integrate seamlessly with several name brand sports watches, but not the off-brand one I am using. I still manually add in my steps to MyNetDiary each day, but I wish that would be automatic. 

Overall I am highly satisfied with this app, and therefore I’m willing to keep paying for it. I do t know how I could do without it after using it so long.

I am a 60-year old female and I’ve lost 17 pounds in the 3 months I’ve been using it. It’s relatively cheap for all the help it’s providing me. Love it!!

Robust app. This app makes calorie counting easy - lots of options for entering food like scanning labels, taking photos and importing recipes. There are automatic settings - for instance, my coffee is automatically logged each day so i don’t have to think about it. Very easy to copy meals from one day to another as well. Finally, the app is smart and calorie allotments adjust with exercise (if you’re connected to a fitness tracker). You also get a weekly review to adjust calorie targets up or down. I’m at a stage of life where it’s very difficult to lose weight so this app has been key to my success.
